name: Mycosis Fungoides

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ISCL/EORTC Diagnostic Criteria for Mycosis Fungoides

criteria.description: Presence of persistent, progressive patches, plaques, or tumors on the skin
Epidermotropism of atypical cerebriform T-lymphocytes on skin biopsy
Loss of pan-T-cell markers (e.g., CD7) and CD4+ T-cell predominance
Detection of T-cell receptor gene rearrangement clonality
Chronicity of skin lesions typically over months to years

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features plus histopathological confirmation and immunophenotyping consistent with MF
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular studies support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent erythematous patches with fine scaling
Plaques with epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes

occasional.symptomName: Erosions or ulcerations of skin lesions

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear may show Sézary cells in advanced disease
imaging: CT scan for lymph node and visceral involvement
PET scan to assess extent of disease
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating epidermotropism and Pautrier microabscesses
Immunohistochemistry showing CD4+ T-cell predominance with loss of CD7

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of atypical lymphocytes on biopsy
Pruritic, inflamed patches with spongiosis on biopsy
Lack of epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes

redFlags: Rapid progression from patches to tumors
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.

Kim YH, Liu HL, Mraz-Gernhard S, Varghese A, Hoppe RT. Long-term outcome of 525 patients with mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome: clinical prognostic factors and risk for disease progression. Arch Dermatol. 2003;139(7):857-866.
Guitart J, Pulitzer M, Duvic M. Mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome: clinical presentation, diagnosis, and staging. UpToDate. 2023.
